Context: a later addition, kept in double brackets (high confidence). 7:53-8:11 is absent from P66, P75, Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, W and the earliest versions; no Greek Father comments on it before the 12th century; its vocabulary is Lukan; and manuscripts place it variously (after John 7:36, 7:44 or 21:25, or Luke 21:38). 7:52 flows into 8:12. Most scholars see an old, possibly genuine story, not John's text. Other possible meanings: (1) part of John's original Gospel — TR/Majority (from Codex D, c. 400, onward), Vulgate (Jerome included it), Augustine, who thought some removed it for fear of moral laxity; KJV, NKJV; (2) an early, authentic story about Jesus later inserted into John — Papias (via Eusebius), the Didascalia, most scholars; printed bracketed in ESV, NIV, NASB, CSB.
